key_insight: A three-level optimization pipeline outperforms per-matrix SVD truncation by jointly refining compressed weights at the matrix, block, and full-model levels.
engineering_relevance: For low-rank LLM compression, optimizing only each matrix is insufficient; block- and model-level refinement can dramatically improve perplexity at the same compression ratio.
method: L1: whitened SVD truncation on individual matrices
L2: joint optimization within Transformer blocks to regularize compounded errors
L3: end-to-end language-model loss refinement using only 256 calibration sequences
evidence_signal: On LLaMA-7B at 60% compression, WikiText-2 perplexity improved from 42.1 after L1 to 19.1 after L2 and 11.4 after L3, with gains reported across 20-80% compression and up to 13B parameters.
watch_item: Reported gains are primarily in perplexity/compression fidelity; downstream task accuracy remains well below the dense model, and cross-architecture results use architecture-specific settings rather than one common protocol.
paper_title: Per-Matrix Optimality Is Not Enough: Three-Level Optimization for Low-Rank LLM Compression
